mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 2.5% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium, pushing S&P 500 forward returns positive over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 2.5% in a single month
regime_hint: preemptive inflation surprise in a low-rate environment
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, 20-day forward returns do not outperform a 2% inflation baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: Rising employment momentum as measured by PAYEMS exceeding 130,000 new jobs per month is associated with stronger consumer confidence and higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next month (5 trading days).
failure_condition: During triggered months, 20-day forward returns remain negative despite a +0.5% one-month average monthly payroll growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO falling below 80) indicates weakening manufacturing momentum, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: During confirmed contractionary INDPRO regimes, 20-day forward returns are not statistically worse than during expansion (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in home sales (HOUST) above 5,000 units signals resilient consumer demand, which elevates S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days regardless of interest rates.
failure_condition: During triggered periods, 20-day forward returns fail to beat the prior month's average (rolling 30-day IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25 percentage points in a single month, the equity risk premium is expected to compress, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25pp in a month
failure_condition: During tightening events, 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during prior easing (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE below 4.5%) accompanied by a simultaneous rise in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS > 120,000) creates a dual labor strength signal that predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: During combined trigger events, 20-day forward returns do not beat a 1% risk premium baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining industrial production (INDPRO < previous month for two months) indicate a supply-side recession, forecasting negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous_month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During such regimes, 20-day forward returns are not statistically worse than during normal expansion (rolling IC > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in RSAFS below 300 million dollars for three consecutive months signals excess liquidity in the financial system, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next month (5 trading days).
failure_condition: During triggered months, 20-day forward returns do not exceed the prior month's average (rolling IC < 0.03).
